relations.legacyQuote: Representation: Fixed length of six digits
relations.reason: Both state the six-digit representation of Element 86. Allocation range, uniqueness, lifecycle association and nonfinancial segment applicability are separate obligations; only this scoped representation core is equivalent.
The legacy BR combines width and lifecycle persistence. Width alone cannot replace or satisfy the entire compound legacy BR.
The follow-up persistence proposition is only the lifecycle component of a legacy width-and-persistence BR.
The legacy BR also requires approval context. Sequence equality does not prove approval-reference correctness or transaction eligibility.
Authorization completion specializes associated follow-up persistence; the completion must independently be eligible and correlated to the original authorization.
Authorization void specializes associated follow-up persistence; equality is not evidence that void is supported.
The legacy statement refers to a return, while the newer quoted general rule refers to an initial authorization. No automatic inheritance to a return lifecycle is justified.
A sale void is not automatically an authorization follow-up in every profile. Retain the distinct precondition pending transaction-family source review.
The timed-out request need not be an initial authorization. The broader timeout rule cannot be merged with authorization-associated persistence.

relations.legacyQuote: These specifications do not support Return transactions.
relations.reason: Both prohibit eWIC Return. The prohibition belongs to the eWIC transaction context, not merely to the presence of Segment 103. Reversal/Void and cancellation remain distinct permitted operations.
The no-Return prohibition is only one part of a larger segment-applicability matrix; it does not establish required/optional Segment 103 status for other transaction types.
Blocking subsequent transactions until receipt of the reversal response is the lifecycle component; the legacy BR additionally requires prompt code 8086.
The missing-expiration default 1249 is shared in the manual loyalty context. The legacy BR additionally specifies numeric four-character MMYY representation when populated.
Three-byte representation and conditional supply from the chip are separate assertions. Width alone does not prove tag presence, zero-padding, blank fill or correct origin.

SCAN/TeleCheck swipe capture requires MICR, while the legacy Segment 110 BR also specifies representation, truncation and overflow routing for check transactions. Capture and encoding are not equivalent.
The Certegy manual-check narrative supplies a program-specific DOB trigger missing from the segment-table-only legacy statement; eight-digit encoding and other programs still require separate review.
The precondition for using an activated account is not equivalent to the behavior of the activation transaction. Activation must not itself be blocked for an inactive card.
Skipping expiration in WEX Money Code processing is narrower than omitting all discretionary data for several card types. Neither statement replaces the other.

Visa incremental authorization is a conditional instance of initial-authorization sequence persistence. This relation does not add a separately approved denominator unit or establish Visa eligibility.
Credit default Track 2 and PINless magnetic-stripe Track 2 share an outcome, but have different routing, eligibility and fallback conditions. No shared-outcome merge.
Credit expiration validation and EBT no device validation are context-specific policies, not conflicting requirements in one context. Prompting/defaulting remains separate.
Ordinary barcode gift cards and Blackhawk scanned gift cards have distinct entry modes. The explicit Blackhawk exception must survive canonicalization.
WEX fleet connection-loss storage responsibility cannot inherit COMDATA Fleet's Store-and-Forward prohibition. The Petroleum source versions and program conditions remain separate.
WEX OTR prohibits manual entry whereas WEX Money Code requires it. These separate program profiles must not inherit a single generic WEX entry rule.
